end.summary:
Reyansh described growing patterns and used rules such as 2n + 1 and 3n + 1 in examples; this was shown on a why/new-situation check.
They practised substituting values into rules to find far terms and test pattern membership; this is still to be checked next time.
They identified that Raj’s n + 3 rule did not fit the pattern and suggested 3n + 1 instead.
The step-change-versus-algebraic-rule mix-up appeared again with n + 4 and n + 3, so it was not corrected by the end.
end.parentNote: Asha practised describing growing patterns with Reyansh, including noticing the separate starting term in rules such as 2n + 1. They also practised substituting a term number into a rule and checking whether a number belongs to a pattern; far-term and membership questions still need more practice. The mix-up between the step-to-step change and the full algebraic rule came up again at the end. At home, show a short pattern and ask, “What changes each time?” and “What rule gives the nth term?” before calculating a far term.
